overall: As of late morning in Washington, DC, temperatures have stalled around 80-81°F under broken cloud cover with a low ceiling (~762m) and 100% cloud fraction, which is suppressing the typical daytime heating ramp. A high dewpoint of 71.6°F, easterly flow, and nearby flood advisories/flash flood warnings signal a moisture-laden, convectively active environment that could further cap afternoon temperatures if storms develop.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is unusually wide: NBM (80.8°F) is highly conservative and nearly matches current conditions, ECMWF (82.5°F) and NWS (84°F) are moderate, while GFS (85.4°F) and especially HRRR (87.4°F) are notably more aggressive. The INTRADAY model's bullish 88-91°F signals appear at odds with the stalled velocity (+0.0°F/hr), negative acceleration (-0.9°F/hr²), and dense cloud cover currently observed.
max_temp_prediction: Despite the predicted peak hour of ~15:30 ET suggesting several hours of heating remain, the combination of thick cloud cover, moist easterly flow, stalled intraday warming, and active convective threat strongly favors the conservative-to-moderate model camp. The NWS official forecast of 84°F is well-anchored and aligns closely with ECMWF/GFS; the active Kalshi even-bucket top at 88-89°F (34.8%) appears overconfident given current surface conditions. Best estimate is the 84-85°F even bucket, with moderate confidence.
